name: Meeting Checklist
description: A before, during, and after checklist for meetings that actually get things done.

sections.title: Decide If You Need a Meeting

items.text: Confirm the goal can't be handled by a message or document
Define the single outcome the meeting must achieve
Choose the shortest time that fits the goal
items.note: Try 25 or 50 minutes to leave a buffer between calls.

items.text: Invite only the people who decide or contribute
Pick a time that respects attendees' schedules
List each topic as a question or decision to make
Assign a time estimate and an owner to each item
Order topics by priority in case time runs short
Note any pre-reading or prep attendees need
Send the agenda at least a day in advance
Confirm attendance and reschedule if key people can't join
Book the room or set up the video link
Test screen sharing, audio, and any equipment
items.note: A two-minute tech check prevents lost minutes.

items.text: Gather documents, slides, or data you will present
Assign someone to take notes
Start on time and restate the goal and agenda
Keep each topic within its time box
Encourage quieter attendees to contribute
Park off-topic items in a separate list
items.note: A parking lot keeps the agenda moving.

items.text: Summarize decisions out loud before moving on
End by recapping action items and owners
Write each action as a clear, specific task
Assign one owner to every action item
Set a due date for each task
Record decisions made during the meeting
Note any open questions to resolve later
Send notes and action items within a day
Add tasks to your team's tracker or tool
Share decisions with people who couldn't attend
Check in on progress before the next meeting
items.note: A quick nudge keeps action items from stalling.

items.text: Schedule any needed follow-up session

faq.a: A clear purpose, a focused agenda, the right people, time-boxed discussion, and documented action items with owners. Effective meetings end with decisions, not just conversation.

faq.q: What should a meeting agenda include?
faq.a: The meeting goal, the topics to cover with time estimates, who leads each item, and any prep attendees need to do beforehand. Send it in advance so people arrive ready.

faq.q: How do I keep a meeting on track?
faq.a: Start on time, follow the agenda, time-box each topic, and park off-topic items for later. Restate decisions and next steps before moving on so nothing is lost.

faq.q: What should I do after a meeting?
faq.a: Send notes with decisions and action items, assign an owner and due date to each task, and follow up before the next meeting to confirm progress.

faq.q: Can I print this meeting checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Download the printable PDF, keep it handy while you plan and host, and check off each step before, during, and after every meeting.
